clue.text: Alsatians worried the attacker

indicators.note: worried in the sense of harassed and shaken about, so the dogs' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pack of guard dogs is being blamed for savaging someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like the dogs fretting, but it is the anagram signal: ALSATIANS rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attacks another person is their assailant, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Push a boy and disturbing behaviour will be the result

parts.note: to ram is to push hard
a page is a boy servant or attendant

explanation.surface: Shoving a youngster around will lead to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a boy' together gives PAGE, a pageboy; 'and ... will be the result' only joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, destructive spree is violent, disturbing conduct.

clue.text: Spot outside right one is marking

indicators.note: outside says the word for spot goes round the other letters

parts.note: a station is a spot or position someone is posted to
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spot just beyond the right-hand edge counts as a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts STATION around R and I, splitting it as ST-RI-ATION; 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Striations are fine lines or grooves, a kind of marking on a surface.

clue.text: Put out more than anticipated on account of the children

parts.note: over can mean concerning or on account of, as in a quarrel over money
issue is a formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: Someone spent more than planned because of their kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests spending, but here it means issuing, as a bank puts out notes or shares.
explanation.definitionFit: To overissue is to release more notes, shares or stock than was intended or allowed.

clue.text: Gold trade-a very tough business

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: Dealing in gold is described as a hard line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, testing experience, something very hard to go through.

clue.text: Game allowed to get in the way

indicators.note: to get in says the word for allowed is placed inside the way

parts.note: a route is a way to go
let means allowed, as in let through

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to obstruct the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in the way' reads as one idea, obstruction, but it splits: 'to get in' is the container signal and 'the way' is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino gambling game with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: A remover shuffled his feet, an indication of indecisiveness

parts.note: to shift is to move about restlessly, shuffling one's feet
er is the sound someone makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: A removal man fidgets uneasily, unable to make up his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffled' looks like an anagram signal, but the phrase 'shuffled his feet' as a whole gives SHIFT; ER is the hesitant noise people make.
explanation.definitionFit: A shifter is someone who moves things about, as a furniture remover or scene-shifter does.

clue.text: Finding French article really good about deputy-head being on the wat side

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
A1 means first-rate, with the figure 1 written as the letter I
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: head here means the first letter of deputy

explanation.surface: Someone praises a deputy head, who turns out to be a bit damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deputy-head' looks like a school's second-in-command but means D, the first letter of deputy. A1 (excellent) is taken as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes left unaired have not been dried out properly, so they remain slightly damp.

clue.text: Bearing with a mad character's crack

parts.note: a compass bearing such as south gives S
the Mad Hatter, from Alice in Wonderland, gives the proverbially mad hatter

explanation.surface: A remark about the way a lunatic carries himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' suggests posture but is a compass point, S; the 's is 'is', linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something is to break it, as to shatter is to smash it.

clue.text: A strict moralist who's put Iran to rights

indicators.note: putting something to rights means sorting it out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stern moral reformer has gone to sort out Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put Iran to rights' rearranges PUTIRAN; 'who's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Puritans were austere Protestants; the word now describes anyone rigidly moral.

clue.text: Give information to coppers in a force

indicators.note: in places the coppers inside the remaining letters

parts.note: to prise is to force open with a lever
coppers are small coins, pence, abbreviated p

explanation.surface: Police officers are being briefed within a constabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police and 'force' a police force, but they are pence (P) and PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone of a fact is to notify them, the meaning of apprise.

clue.text: Those raising no objection when a fool gets in

parts.note: an ass is a fool
enters means gets in

explanation.surface: Nobody objects when an idiot gets elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: People who agree to a proposal, giving their consent.

clue.text: A coastal area some choose as ideal for retirement

indicators.note: some indicates only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Many people pick the shore as the best place to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'choose as ideal'; 'for retirement' completes the picture only.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is land by the sea, a coastal district or resort.

clue.text: Lie heard-a story — at the bar one may expect that

definitions.text: at the bar one may expect that

indicators.note: heard says the word lie is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: lie, said aloud, is the opening sound of the beer's first word
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub tells a fib and spins a yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'lie tale' runs together into the beer's name; the definition plays on what a drinker might order over the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Light ale is a pale bottled beer commonly served in British pubs.

clue.text: Soldiers involved in the current fulmination

indicators.note: involved in says the soldiers are placed inside the current

parts.note: a tide is a current of water
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Troops caught up in the latest outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective meaning present, but it is a flow of water, TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a thundering denunciation.

clue.text: Sandwich material

definitions.meaning: to sandwich something is to insert it between other layers or lines
the extra lining fabric put between the outer cloth and lining of a garment

explanation.definitionFit: To interline is to insert between lines or layers, and also to give a garment an extra stiffening lining.

clue.text: No longer single-speed, that's clear

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former, no longer
one means single
rate is speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A bike that's no longer a one-gear model has been given the all-clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single-speed' reads as one bicycle term but gives two pieces, ONE and RATE; 'that's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of blame.

clue.text: They're prepared for a row whenever they meet

definitions.text: They're prepared for a row whenever they meet

parts.words: They're prepared for a row whenever they meet
parts.note: sounds like quarrelsome people, but row means a stretch of rowing, as for a crew who meet to take out a boat

explanation.definitionFit: Rowers in a crew gather to row together.

clue.text: Sportsmen may be the least affected

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps the fittest people are those least troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges THELEAST; 'may be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes are people who compete in sports, especially track and field.

clue.text: Possibly showing latent ability

indicators.note: possibly suggests another possible version of the word, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone may be displaying hidden gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges LATENT; 'showing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is natural skill or aptitude.

clue.text: Spirited instruction guiding the players

parts.note: a marking in a musical score that tells performers to play in a lively way

explanation.definitionFit: Animato is an Italian musical direction meaning play with animation.

clue.text: Not slow to give voice

definitions.meaning: fast, as a non-stopping train or delivery is
to put thoughts or feelings into words

explanation.definitionFit: An express train is fast; to express an idea is to state it.

clue.text: Writing up different gag

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
other means different

explanation.surface: A new piece of writing about a different joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MS to SM. 'gag' looks like a joke but means to silence.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to stifle them, and to smother is to suppress or muffle.

clue.text: The Northerner living in a depressed area

definitions.text: The Northerner living in a depressed area

parts.words: The Northerner living in a depressed area
parts.note: suggests someone in an economically deprived region, but the area is literally low ground, a valley

explanation.definitionFit: A man from the Yorkshire Dales or similar northern English valleys, dales being low valleys.

clue.text: Stick notice on present

indicators.note: in a down clue on means one piece sits above the other

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
here means present, as at a roll call

explanation.surface: Fix a notice to a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to something.

clue.text: Scattered and disappeared — about time!

indicators.note: about says the word for disappeared goes round the period

parts.note: to die away or die out is to disappear
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone relieved a crowd has finally gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about time!' reads as a sigh of relief, but 'about' is the container signal with 'time' the inner piece; 'and' links. 'Disappeared' means died away, as a sound does.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubts or crowds that are dispelled are driven away and scattered.

clue.text: A music man accompanying the monarch needed to carry a pistol

parts.note: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A musician escorting the Queen had to be armed.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth; 'accompanying' just sets the two side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is the leather case that holds a pistol on a belt.

clue.text: Loftiness can appear fun in spring.

indicators.note: in puts the word for fun inside the word for spring

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a jest is a bit of fun, a joke

explanation.surface: Grandness can seem playful when the season turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can appear' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is stately grandeur, an elevated dignity.

clue.text: The bank set out to be most unpleasant

parts.note: a bank is a row, as of oars or keys, which is a rank

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A financial institution has decided to be as nasty as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money, but it is a row, RANK; 'set out' rearranges SET as EST. 'The' and 'to be' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul or offensive, so rankest is the most offensive.

clue.text: Equine understanding

parts.note: reads as a horse's comprehension, but understanding is taken literally as what stands under a horse

explanation.definitionFit: A curved iron plate nailed beneath a horse's hoof.
